source_claim: A paper claim and locked task can be compiled into a source-anchored obligation graph whose executable deletion tests yield a one-deletion-minimal claim-bearing witness and a direct task-local effect test.

axes.problem: Find the smallest source-grounded operational subset needed to exercise a paper's core claim on the user's task.
axes.mechanism: Typed obligation graph, source and dependency checkers, executable witness predicates, fixed-point block deletion, counterexample traces, and a claim-on versus claim-off local trial.
axes.insight: Field completeness and source support do not establish joint operational sufficiency; every retained obligation should survive a downstream deletion challenge.
axes.application: Paper-to-skill compilation and task-specific minimal reproduction.
axes.evaluation_scope: Eight bounded case studies, deletion controls, local task effect, resource cost, and prospective failure-boundary cases.

comparisons.title: Anything2Skill: Compiling External Knowledge into Reusable Skills for Agents
comparisons.evidence: Anything2Skill compiles evidence windows into structured contracts with actions, constraints, outputs, evidence, and confidence, but does not use downstream deletion to certify joint claim sufficiency.
comparisons.limitations: It defeats broad claims about first evidence-grounded knowledge-to-skill compilation.

comparisons.title: SkillFoundry: Automated Mining and Validation of Agent Skills for Scientific Tasks
comparisons.evidence: SkillFoundry mines operational contracts and closes execution-validation loops, but does not require each retained claim obligation to carry a failed-deletion counterexample.

comparisons.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
comparisons.evidence: PaperBench defines hierarchical author-approved replication requirements and fresh execution, but does not minimize requirements into a source-linked task-local claim witness.
comparisons.limitations: Its rubrics are a strong completeness baseline.

comparisons.title: AutoReproduce: Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
comparisons.evidence: AutoReproduce builds and debugs end-to-end reproductions using sampled validation, rather than deleting non-load-bearing paper obligations to a local fixed point.
comparisons.limitations: It is a stronger complete-reproduction baseline.

comparisons.title: A Minimal Executable Proof for Multi-Language Contract Traceability
comparisons.evidence: The abstract combines an observable-output contract, implementation graph, traceability file, readiness gate, and executable witnesses; it does not derive or minimize obligations from a scientific paper claim.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
Dynamic program slicing, delta debugging, dependency minimization, and minimal-core extraction are high-risk classical ancestors and cannot themselves support novelty.
The combined source-anchored compiler and local claim witness, not deletion minimization alone, is the only defensible delta.
